g.title: seq
g.text: 11b Cash programming: how the amount of cash authority for a period is decided

a.text: 1. DBCC to DBM: Fiscal program of the year:
revenue, disbursements, deficit, financing
2. DBCC to BTr: Same fiscal program, with the
financing program
3. National agency to DBM: Monthly
Disbursement Program (BED 3) through URS
4. DBM to BTr: Disbursement program of the
government, by month
5. DOF to BTr: Revenue forecast, by month
6. BTr: Cash forecast for the next three
months, updated regularly
7. BTr: Plan the borrowing schedule and the
placement of surplus cash
8. DBM to Servicing banks: NCA for the
quarter, per agency, by month
13. National agency to DBM: Monthly Report of
Disbursements (FAR 4)
9. Servicing banks to BTr: Payments made on
agency orders
10. BTr to Treasury Single Account: Replenish
the servicing banks
11. Agent banks and gateways to Treasury
Single Account: Collections of BIR and BOC
arrive through collecting banks
12. BTr: Check the cash balance against the
forecast
14. DBM: Compare actual payments with the
program

a.xlink:title: skip: Agency spends slower than its program, or cash is not sufficient

a.text: 15. DBM to National agency: Later NCAs
adjusted to spending performance and to the
fiscal position

a.xlink:title: skip: Agency needs more cash than its program

a.text: 16. National agency to DBM: Request for
additional NCA, with justification

a.xlink:title: end of: Agency spends slower than its program, or cash is not sufficient

a.text: 17. BTr to DBCC: Monthly Cash Operations
Report: revenue, disbursements, surplus or
deficit, financing

a.xlink:title: end of: Agency needs more cash than its program
